1: # CS5351 agent entry point
2: 
3: Build target: extend the existing single-stock TradingAgents application for FR-01–FR-03 and NFR-01–NFR-02. The unchanged reference is `upstream-baseline` at `9fa1196fffbcfd9de5146d2dd2869df84ab99838`. Preserve `tradingagents/`, `cli/` and the existing test suite; add course tests under `test/offline/` and `test/live/`.
4: 
5: Documentation: [index](docs/README.md), [C0–C5 contracts](docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md) and [review records](docs/review-memo.md). Use the approved specification revision. Report missing allowlist paths to the human maintainer before the affected operation.
6: 
7: Read in order: [D1 registry](docs/req/requirements.yaml), [blueprint](architecture-blueprint.md), [ADR](docs/architecture/adr/001-choice-tbd.md), [invariants](docs/architecture/invariants.md), [trace matrix](docs/architecture/trace-matrix.md), [state](docs/architecture/memory-design.md), [permissions](docs/architecture/permission-model.md), [runtime policies](docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md), [candidate evaluation](docs/architecture/evaluation-table.md), then [structural constraints](docs/code-governance/structural-constraints.md), [tool rules](docs/code-governance/mcp-tool-manifest.md) and [covenant](.agent/rules.md).
8: 
9: After reading this entry point, follow [Prompt.md](Prompt.md) as the shared launch prompt. Plan first: name requirements and invariants, list exact files and contracts, specify independent normal/negative tests and rollback. Stop for recorded human approval of plan and tests before generating any implementation. Use the approved path list on each tool request. Configured writable paths are an outer limit; task approval may narrow them further. Governance, baseline history, existing tests and external data are frozen to the agent.
10: 
11: Verify imports and module boundaries, baseline regressions, each fit criterion and safety counterexamples. Offline runs use fixed fixtures and fake transport; live checks are separate and human-run. Record commands/results and actual interventions; mark unrun checks honestly. Submit a proposed change for human review; never merge, publish or widen permissions yourself.
12: 
13: Coordination: one owner per requirement and an explicitly agreed integrator for shared files. Follow the course OpenCode implementation workflow. Keep preparation/review distinct from implementation evidence and record the actual tools, scopes and sessions in the AI-use log. No auxiliary workflow may bypass course-role restrictions.

1: # D9 — OpenCode launch prompt
2: 
3: Read `AGENTS.md` first, then this prompt and the referenced D1–D4 documents in the order prescribed by `AGENTS.md`. Use the course permission configuration and the current approved requirement and architecture revisions. This is the common launch prompt for all five requirements. The human specifies the requirement IDs, working revision and task scope in the session. If any are missing or the documents conflict, ask for clarification and stop. A request to implement a feature is not approval to begin coding.
4: 
5: ## Gate 1 — Plan and stop (`course-plan`)
6: 
7: Work read-only. Produce an execution plan covering:
8: 
9: 1. **Traceability:** map every selected D1 acceptance criterion and applicable invariant to its D2 component and planned test. Identify any affected shared boundary.
10: 2. **Interface contracts:** specify inputs, outputs, error states and ownership of each decision. Explain how the design preserves deterministic publication and dispatch rules where applicable.
11: 3. **Scope:** list the exact files to read and change, which baseline code must remain intact, and any explicit exclusions. Identify dependencies on other requirements. Never request broader permissions as a shortcut.
12: 4. **Verification:** specify fixed inputs, expected outcomes and commands for normal cases, negative cases and regressions. Include at least one test that would fail if each affected invariant were bypassed. Say which tests require live services; keep them separate from offline acceptance.
13: 5. **Steps and rollback:** give the order for tests, implementation, integration and self-checks, plus a safe rollback approach.
14: 
15: End with **WAITING FOR PLAN AND TEST APPROVAL**. Do not generate or edit implementation or test code at this gate. The human reviewer records the approved plan, test criteria, exact paths, approver and time. A revision to scope, contracts, invariants or acceptance criteria requires a new plan and approval.
16: 
17: ## Gate 2 — Build only the approved change (`course-build`)
18: 
19: When the human switches to Build, require the approved plan and test reference; do not infer approval from a role switch. Have the human approve allowed edits against the exact reviewed paths. Write only the approved tests first. Ask the human to run them against the pre-change behavior and confirm that the key missing-behavior case fails for the expected reason. Stop for human confirmation of that result before editing production code.
20: 
21: Implement the smallest change that satisfies the approved plan. Respect module boundaries, keep the upstream baseline and existing tests intact, and leave governance, CI and permissions to the human. Do not weaken a test to pass or circumvent a rejected edit. If a new dependency, broader path, changed contract or test change is needed, explain it and stop for review.
22: 
23: Summarize the changes, unresolved risks and D4 checks the human should run. End with **WAITING FOR VERIFICATION EVIDENCE**. Do not use shell or external tools.
24: 
25: ## Gate 3 — Self-check and review (`course-verify`)
26: 
27: Work read-only. Inspect the diff or changed files supplied by the human and map each actual result to its planned check. Request human-run structural checks, earlier regression suites and the affected behavioral and invariant checks. Require normal positive controls and adverse cases; keep unavailable, skipped or unrun checks distinct from passes. For application prompt/model changes, request the agreed fixed semantic evaluation evidence before recommending approval.
28: 
29: Return a proposed review summary: requirement IDs, reviewed revision, tests and results, unmet criteria, risks and recommended verdict. Stop for human review. If evidence shows a defect, propose a repair and repeat the appropriate approval and verification gates. Only the human makes the final verdict and controls Git, publishing and merge.
30: 
31: Keep the actual session and mark human interruptions, redirects, approvals and rejections with their rationale. Give the human a summary for the review memo and AI-use log. Never invent evidence, and keep credentials, student identifiers and raw sessions out of the public repository.
32: 
33: ## Task header and handoff required before Gate 1
34: 
35: The human supplies: selected requirement/invariant IDs; common starting SHA and current feature HEAD; contract revision C0–C5; developer and human reviewer; exact read/edit paths; planned case IDs and fixture revision; Python/dependency and OpenCode versions; offline/live scope; and the place to retain private raw sessions. Missing information is an open item, never filled with a fictional approval.
36: 
37: Read the documentation index, open review items in `docs/review-memo.md`, and `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md`. If required material is denied by the current allowlist, report the exact missing paths and stop for human maintenance. The registry status `proposed` is not Build approval. Freeze shared fields/signatures with affected owners first. Use mocks to develop independently, then require integrated evidence with the real components.
38: 
39: Before production edits, the human approves the exact test-design revision; implementation approval and final PR approval are distinct. An ImportError, dependency failure, absent module or no collected tests is not the required failing-before behavior evidence. Record such setup gaps separately and obtain an approved approach to test the baseline behavior. After any approved fixture/expectation change, record why and renew review rather than silently moving the target.
40: 
41: Only actual actions belong in the session record. Keep planning and document review distinct from OpenCode implementation sessions, and record the actual tool, scope and session reference in the AI-use log. Follow the course OpenCode implementation workflow. This launch prompt does not authorize another tool to bypass denied actions or turn advisory output into human approval.
42: 
43: 
44: ## Applying interface v1.0
45: 
46: Use the named shared records and callable boundaries in C0–C5; do not reopen or invent different field meanings per feature. A task plan lists exact integration adapters and tests the specified compatibility views. Internal class choices may vary without changing shared records. Apply task-specific entry criteria from the review memo; independent offline work may use approved fixtures. A team's confirmation of this document is not automatic approval of every feature plan/test.
47: 
48: Use the approved product run-profile limit and verify outbound attempts at the transport boundary. Distinguish charged safety slots, known sends and unknown delivery in receipts. Diagnostic limits are separate from product acceptance; charged attempts do not establish billed model usage.

1: # Shared interface contracts
2: 
3: Version: 1.0. Status: Proposed. Shared boundaries use JSON-compatible records. Internal dataclasses, TypedDict or Pydantic models may use adapters that preserve these fields and semantics. ADR-001 records the design decision.
4: 
5: ## Ownership and integration
6: 
7: | Contract | Authority | Producers and consumers |
8: | --- | --- | --- |
9: | C0 run identity and outcome | Run coordinator | All five owner modules, CLI, Python, report and memory |
10: | C1 evidence and publication | FR-01 publication gate | Analyst evidence, accepted arguments, candidate, all official sinks |
11: | C2 verified metrics | FR-02 metric registry | Fundamentals inputs, controlled downstream fields and metric table |
12: | C3 sentiment coverage | FR-03 coverage component | Existing source adapters, analyst, state, report and downstream agents |
13: | C4 dispatch budget | NFR-01 request-budget component | Both model tiers and every in-scope transport send |
14: | C5 prepared context | NFR-02 context component | Analyst closure and neutral risk debater, then C4 |
15: 
16: Shared-file integration owner: EverForests. Feature owners submit narrow patches for state, schema, graph/client and reporting adapters. Task plans identify exact paths. The integrator preserves approved contracts across patches; shared files must not be independently replaced by feature branches.
17: 
18: ## C0 — identity, state and errors
19: 
20: Every authoritative record carries `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and `as_of_date`. Evidence and metric IDs are only resolvable inside that run. Never retrieve a matching-looking ID from a previous run. A restarted run gets a new ID. A metered checkpoint resume is disabled until the counter/state restoration contract is implemented and approved.
21: 
22: Keep three concepts separate:
23: 
24: - Execution: RUNNING, COMPLETED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or FAILED. COMPLETED describes the workflow, not approval of a recommendation.
25: - Publication: PENDING, APPROVED or BLOCKED, with reason codes. An official rating is present only on APPROVED.
26: - Data coverage: NO_DATA, PARTIAL_DATA or AVAILABLE for optional sentiment. NO_DATA alone is not a failed run or a publication rejection.
27: 
28: A terminal budget/context failure suppresses the official rating. Valid market/financial evidence can still support publication when sentiment is unavailable, provided C1 passes. Diagnostics are explicitly nonofficial; rejected candidate prose must not leak into an official rating field, final-decision section or decision memory. Fixing a contract requires a versioned D1/D2/test update before dependent work continues.
29: 
30: ## C1 — evidence, accepted arguments and publication
31: 
32: An EvidenceRecord contains `run_id`, `evidence_id`, source kind/vendor, request ticker/window, source locator (URL, document/field or fixture reference), observed period and source content/reference. Assigning an ID does not make empty, failed or unrelated content valid. Missing-source diagnostics can explain absence but are not substantive market evidence.
33: 
34: An AcceptedArgument contains `run_id`, `argument_id`, the claim and a nonempty list of evidence IDs that resolve in the current run. This version verifies reference integrity, not whether a source semantically proves an investment conclusion. A candidate contains an explicit rating and accepted argument IDs. Use the existing five-tier vocabulary: Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell. REVIEW and arbitrary free text are not publishable ratings.
35: 
36: The deterministic gate returns one authoritative PublicationResult: identity, publication status, reasons, approved rating or null, and validated argument/evidence references. Invalid rating uses INVALID_RATING; missing, unknown, cross-run or unaccepted required references use INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Diagnostics may retain rejected values privately, but official consumers receive no rejected rating. All four sinks (CLI, Python result, saved official report, decision memory) consume this same result. Structured output, free-text fallback and streaming/final display paths cannot bypass it.
37: 
38: FR-02 adds verified numerical records; FR-01 must not label arbitrary model prose as verified arithmetic. FR-03 missingness does not automatically invalidate other evidence. The v1 result fields below are common to all sinks; name exact sink adapter edits in the relevant feature plan and test each one.
39: 
40: ## C2 — verified metrics
41: 
42: Input: metric kind (YoY, ratio or signed difference), raw operands, source locators/fields, periods, units/currencies and run identity. Use source precision, preferably Decimal-compatible strings. Output: VERIFIED with immutable `metric_id`, normalized operands, formula, result/unit/period and provenance, or UNVERIFIABLE with a reason and no verified value.
43: 
44: - YoY = 100 * (current / prior - 1); compare the same quarter in adjacent years or comparable full years.
45: - Ratio = 100 * numerator / denominator; record dimensional/unit compatibility and period alignment.
46: - Signed difference = current - reference; preserve sign and price unit.
47: - YoY/ratio denominators must be positive in this release. Reject nonfinite values, absent provenance, incompatible units or incomparable periods.
48: - Percentage tolerance is 0.1 **percentage points**, not relative percent. Price-difference tolerance is 0.01 price units. Preserve calculation precision separately from displayed rounding.
49: 
50: Only the owner registry creates authoritative verified records. Consumers resolve IDs against it; a model-supplied value, changed value, unknown ID or new arbitrary ID must not create verification authority. Retain original records for the run and reject conflicting writes.
51: 
52: Real-company acceptance requires archived source operands and independent recomputation. The AAPL YoY field is `Cost of Revenue`. For its signed price-gap example, `current` is the Bollinger upper band and `reference` is the closing price; reversing these roles negates the result. The formula remains `current - reference`, with no absolute-value conversion. Exact operands and evidence status are in the [D4 AAPL examples](../code-governance/verification-constraints.md#fr-02-aapl-acceptance-examples). Synthetic fixtures verify formulas separately. Basis-point calculations and arbitrary narrative-math parsing are outside scope.
53: 
54: ## C3 — sentiment source coverage and nullable score
55: 
56: Three logical sources are `news`, `stocktwits` and `reddit`; Reddit's three subreddits collectively count as one source. Record the actual news vendor; a configured fallback must not be mislabeled Yahoo. Do not add another data provider. For like-for-like baseline checks, record the chosen vendor route.
57: 
58: Each SourceOutcome contains identity, source ID, requested window, availability, valid-record count, reason codes and shareable evidence locators. A source counts once when it returns at least one substantive item attributable to the requested ticker and valid window. Ticker association may come from explicit item metadata or an approved, request-bound adapter; arbitrary substring matches and model assertions are insufficient. Agree and test the supported adapter metadata/placeholder patterns before implementation. An opaque nonempty string is not automatically valid data.
59: 
60: Use the baseline's seven-day-back start and end date: [start 00:00 UTC, end + 1 day 00:00 UTC). AAPL as-of 2026-11-10 therefore covers 2026-11-03 through 2026-11-10. Freeze the clock for date-dependent fixtures. Historical undated content cannot prove window validity. Do not silently tighten or change the baseline date semantics; document any justified change and test boundaries.
61: 
62: Reasons distinguish at least EMPTY, FETCH_ERROR, WINDOW_UNSUPPORTED, OUT_OF_WINDOW, TICKER_MISMATCH and UNVERIFIABLE_METADATA. Keep actual vendor failure distinct from a successful fetch with no matching items. Never claim these statuses prove that no real-world messages/news exist.
63: 
64: | Valid logical sources | coverage_status | Sentiment output |
65: | --- | --- | --- |
66: | 0/3 | NO_DATA | overall_band UNKNOWN; overall_score null |
67: | 1/3 or 2/3 | PARTIAL_DATA | Coverage remains explicit; any measured score uses valid evidence only |
68: | 3/3 | AVAILABLE | Coverage available; score still requires a valid assessment |
69: 
70: Coverage is authoritative data state; the model cannot increase it. With nonzero coverage, permit a finite 0–10 score and an existing band only when an assessment was produced. If assessment fails or its score is absent/invalid, use UNKNOWN/null while retaining the nonzero coverage and an assessment-failure reason; do not mislabel this NO_DATA. A genuine measured Neutral/5.0 remains legal.
71: 
72: Missing scores never become 0 or 5 and never enter a numerical mean. Structured state, analyst message, downstream prompt and persisted/rendered report must agree. Handle nullable scores without numeric-format errors. Apply the contract to structured **and** free-text fallback; model narrative cannot override authoritative coverage. Keep the existing sentiment_report text as a compatibility view; the new sentiment_assessment record below is authoritative. Both must agree. Internal schema adaptation may change, but the v1 shared record does not drift silently.
73: 
74: The original baseline stores `sentiment_report` as text and requires a nonnull numeric SentimentReport score. Updating only the prompt cannot establish this contract. No raw social bodies or credentials belong in public evidence. Missing optional sentiment does not stop otherwise valid market/fundamental analysis; C1 still decides publication.
75: 
76: ## C4 — atomic per-run model dispatch
77: 
78: Supported scope: one single-stock main analysis, both model tiers, structured/fallback requests and application retries. Count actual outgoing model attempts, not nodes, tool invocations, callbacks or tokens. Historical settlement is excluded. Disable SDK/transport implicit retries in supported course runs; unsupported hidden-retry modes are outside the verified configuration, not silently compliant.
79: 
80: Budget state: positive integer `limit`, charged sends, active reservations and exhaustion. Atomically reserve capacity before a send so charged sends plus active reservations cannot exceed limit. A reservation transitions once to a charged attempt at the outbound boundary. A provider error after an attempted send consumes the slot; do not refund an ambiguous send. A cancellation proven to precede transport may release an unused reservation. Validate C5 first so context rejection obtains no reservation.
81: 
82: No slot => BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, no request, no official recommendation. Limit 3 allows exactly 3 attempts; the fourth is refused. Concurrent runs do not share counters. Include application fallback/retry attempts separately. C4 does not promise a monetary or token cap. Transport probes must count actual fake sends and check reservation cleanup rather than trusting the reported counter alone.
83: 
84: ## C5 — deterministic prepared context
85: 
86: Initial integration sites: analyst closure and `risk_mgmt/neutral_debator.py` only. Other analyst turns and risk roles are not implicitly covered. Before reserving C4, fully expand/convert the scoped final message sequence into one agreed provider-facing representation.
87: 
88: Canonical v1 measurement: the final provider-facing message array encoded as JSON with ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon) without optional whitespace, allow_nan=False, then UTF-8. Use the ChatMessage representation below and freeze byte fixtures before implementation. Do not measure before template expansion or change representation after measuring. Tool schemas and other separately bound fields are excluded from this message metric and must be recorded/bounded separately; this is not a cap on the whole HTTP body.
89: 
90: Required blocks: role/task identity; standing safety/publication rules; ticker/date/run identity; current required evidence/verified metrics/source coverage; and the active tool-call/result exchange. Optional blocks: explicitly marked older discussion/history. A tool-call/result pair is indivisible; if a member is required, preserve the whole pair. Text-wrapped tools retain name, arguments and corresponding result. Removing context cannot delete authoritative evidence/state from storage.
91: 
92: At the configured 65536-byte acceptance cap: short input passes unchanged. If oversized, remove optional groups oldest first (stable original index for ties), reassemble, reinject critical constraints and remeasure. Do not summarize required evidence with another unmetered model call. If required blocks cannot fit or pairing cannot be preserved, return CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE; zero send, reservation and debit. Same normalized input/config produces identical prepared output. Run final retention/pairing checks before C4.
93: 
94: This byte cap does not implement the separate D2 token-budget requirement. ADR-001 records that architecture design and the remaining tokenizer/model-capacity validation. Do not infer token counts from bytes/4 or claim provider safety from 64 KiB alone.
95: 
96: ## Contract-change and approval record
97: 
98: Before implementation, record requirement IDs, contract revision, baseline SHA, exact read/edit paths, fixture/case revision, reviewer and approval time. The human approval record identifies the reviewed revision and scope. Reapprove changes to shared fields, thresholds, test expectations, safety paths or dependencies. Feature PRs link the approved plan and actual evidence; the coordinator runs integrated regressions before release.
99: 
100: 
101: ## V1 shared record layout
102: 
103: Version field: `contract_version = "1.0"`. Shared artifacts carry `run_id`, normalized `ticker` and ISO `as_of_date` copied from RunContext. Nonsecret IDs are opaque strings; consumers must not infer meaning from their spelling. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. A missing optional value is explicit null; a missing required field is an invalid record. Lists have deterministic order; ID-indexed registries are mappings, not unordered output prose.
104: 
105: | Record | Required shared fields beyond identity | Owner |
106: | --- | --- | --- |
107: | RunContext | contract_version, execution_status, request_limit (positive integer) | Existing graph/run entry; integration by coordinator |
108: | EvidenceRecord | evidence_id, source_kind, vendor, source_ref, content_ref, window_start, window_end | FR-01 collection/index adapter |
109: | AcceptedArgument | argument_id, claim (nonempty text), evidence_ids (nonempty list) | FR-01 validates against run-local evidence; a model flag is not acceptance |
110: | CandidateDecision | rating (untrusted string or null), argument_ids | Model/adapters produce; C1 decides |
111: | PublicationResult | publication_status, reason_codes, rating (allowed string or null), argument_ids, evidence_ids | FR-01 |
112: | Operand | role, value (finite decimal string), unit, period, source_ref, field_ref | FR-02 input adapter; roles current/prior/numerator/denominator/reference |
113: | MetricRequest | kind (yoy/ratio/price_delta), operands | FR-02 input |
114: | VerifiedMetric | metric_id, kind, operands, result_value (decimal string), result_unit, formula, source_refs | FR-02 immutable run-local registry |
115: | MetricResult | status (VERIFIED/UNVERIFIABLE), metric (VerifiedMetric or null), reason_codes | FR-02 |
116: | SourceOutcome | source_id, window_start, window_end, available (bool), valid_record_count, reason_codes, evidence_refs | FR-03 normalization adapter |
117: | SentimentCoverage | coverage_status, valid_sources, total_sources (=3), sources (mapping keyed news/stocktwits/reddit) | FR-03 deterministic coverage |
118: | SentimentAssessment | all SentimentCoverage fields, assessment_status (MEASURED/UNKNOWN), overall_band, overall_score, confidence, assessment_reason_codes, narrative | FR-03 deterministic finalization |
119: | ContextBlock | group_id, required (bool), messages (list of ChatMessage); grouping metadata is never sent to the model | NFR-02 scoped adapter |
120: | PreparedRequest | status (READY/CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE), messages (list or null), message_bytes, original_message_bytes, dropped_group_ids, required_groups_ok | NFR-02 or nonreducing adapter |
121: | Reservation | reservation_id, run_id, state (reserved/charged/cancelled); opaque to other features | NFR-01 |
122: 
123: `Operand.period` is `{kind, start, end, label}`: kind is quarter/year/instant, start/end are ISO dates, and label records the source's fiscal period or quote timestamp. Currency and scale are part of unit (for example USD vs USD_millions); conversion must be explicit and preserve original operands. Do not silently take abs(capex), invent comparable periods or round source values to make a fixture match. An EvidenceRecord source_ref identifies the source, while content_ref locates the retained shareable material/fixture; an ID with no resolvable retained material is insufficient.
124: 
125: For SentimentAssessment, overall_band is one existing measured band or UNKNOWN. overall_score is a finite float in [0,10] for MEASURED, otherwise null. confidence keeps the existing low/medium/high vocabulary; UNKNOWN uses low and is not a measured weak-neutral signal. Missing sources are unavailable with reasons; valid sources have valid_record_count >=1. Missing uncollected source entries are normalized as unavailable with NOT_COLLECTED rather than increasing the denominator or silently disappearing. Extra providers do not count as fourth sources. Source order is news, stocktwits, reddit.
126: 
127: `ChatMessage` contains provider-facing role, content and, when present, name/tool_call_id/tool_calls/reasoning_content. Preserve content strings or JSON-compatible content blocks without paraphrasing. Preserve each tool call's id, type, function name and arguments plus the paired tool result. Reasoning fields required by the selected provider's tool round-trip are mandatory if present. Do not add ContextBlock metadata to ChatMessage. The cap measures the agreed canonical message representation, not HTTP whitespace, the whole body, output tokens or hidden provider overhead.
128: 
129: ## V1 callable boundaries (specification signatures, no implementation)
130: 
131: Inputs are read-only to consumers. Return the declared records; do not attach extra authoritative fields through prose. Signatures below describe Python-callable boundaries; they do not create five network services.
132: 
133: | Planned owner | Public v1 call | Behavior |
134: | --- | --- | --- |
135: | publication_gate.py | validate_argument(argument, evidence_index, run) -> AcceptedArgument or validation failure | Check current-run references before acceptance |
136: | publication_gate.py | evaluate_publication(candidate, argument_index, evidence_index, run) -> PublicationResult | Recheck accepted references and rating; one result for all official sinks |
137: | verified_metrics.py | verify_metric(request, run) -> MetricResult | Compute from validated operands, register only verified records |
138: | verified_metrics.py | resolve_metric(metric_id, registry, run) -> VerifiedMetric or null | Resolve trusted ID; never accept a caller-supplied replacement value |
139: | sentiment_coverage.py | normalize_source(raw_result, source_id, run, window_start, window_end) -> SourceOutcome | Derive availability from collection receipts and approved metadata rules |
140: | sentiment_coverage.py | build_sentiment_coverage(sources, run) -> SentimentCoverage | Count three logical sources once each |
141: | sentiment_coverage.py | finalize_sentiment(coverage, model_assessment_or_null, run) -> SentimentAssessment | Coverage is authoritative; validate score/band; no imputation |
142: | context_limit.py | prepare_context(blocks, max_message_bytes=65536) -> PreparedRequest | Only the two scoped sites reduce; reject irreducible context |
143: | request_budget.py | RequestBudget(run_id, limit); try_reserve() -> Reservation or null; charge_attempt(ticket); cancel_before_send(ticket); snapshot() | Atomic lifecycle; cancellation only when transport is known not to have started |
144: | request_budget.py | dispatch(prepared, budget, send) -> sender's normal response type | Require READY, reserve, charge at attempt boundary, invoke send exactly once; refusal is a typed failure, never a Hold/default rating |
145: 
146: The sender callable accepts the prepared messages and performs exactly one underlying request with SDK retries disabled. Application fallback/retries call dispatch again. Dispatch failure types are BudgetExhausted, ContextTooLarge and ProviderFailure (defined in the responsible owner module); the graph entry maps them to C0 terminal state. Provider failures after an ambiguous attempt remain charged. Snapshot separates charged attempts, known actual sends and unknown-delivery attempts; a connection attempt is not claimed to be a billed model response.
147: 
148: Publication evaluation first respects C0 terminal failure/incomplete execution (BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE or RUN_NOT_COMPLETE); then rejects an invalid rating; then rejects insufficient references. APPROVED has an allowed rating, nonempty accepted argument/evidence references and no rejection reasons. BLOCKED always has rating=null. An incomplete workflow cannot publish an earlier candidate.
149: 
150: ## V1 graph handoff and compatibility
151: 
152: Add the following keys to the existing AgentState through narrow integration edits: course_run (RunContext), evidence_index, argument_index, verified_metrics, sentiment_assessment and publication_result. These are separate state keys; do not have parallel nodes overwrite an entire common nested dictionary. Existing nodes own their existing report strings. New owner records are not reconstructed from those strings. Avoid new dependencies or replacement of the orchestrator.
153: 
154: For sentiment, the analyst emits sentiment_assessment and renders its legacy sentiment_report from that same record, including the model-message/report views. At 0/3, the selected v1 path skips the sentiment model call and creates a deterministic missing-data narrative with UNKNOWN/null. With data, finalize the model assessment while preserving coverage; provider/free-text fallback cannot restore a made-up default score. The FR-03 task plan tests schema/renderer compatibility before selecting the internal Pydantic adaptation. FR-01 can publish from valid non-sentiment evidence when its own gate passes.
155: 
156: The shared model client receives PreparedRequest. At the two NFR-02 sites use prepare_context; elsewhere use a nonreducing READY adapter so NFR-01 covers all sends without accidentally applying a 64 KiB cap to every call. All branches then use the same C4 dispatch boundary. Tests can use fixed fake producers/consumers until integration, but combined graph acceptance needs the real connected owner modules.
157: 
158: ## Working defaults and limits with different purposes
159: 
160: | Setting | V1 choice / purpose | Change rule |
161: | --- | --- | --- |
162: | Application baseline | 9fa1196; retain existing package layout | New baseline needs explicit rationale and regressions |
163: | Local environment | Reuse verified Python 3.11 environment; record exact patch/dependencies | Align a team-approved baseline when needed, no automatic reinstall |
164: | Course profile model | School CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash for both tiers; explicit thinking-disabled request after compatibility check | Record actual settings; do not infer backend revision from alias |
165: | Course profile output allowance | 4096 tokens as initial run-profile choice, not an acceptance threshold | Raise only with a truncation reason and recorded configuration |
166: | Product request_limit | 40 per single-stock run as initial configurable profile | Revisit against completed baseline; D1 hard rule is actual requests <= configured limit |
167: | NFR-01 boundary fixture | limit 3, exactly-three succeeds, fourth refuses | Fixed test condition; not the normal application's default |
168: | NFR-02 message cap | 65536 bytes at analyst closure and neutral risk role | Normal configurable setting; changes update the affected fixtures/contracts |
169: | Token architecture proposal | 16384 input tokens, 80% trigger remains unactivated design pending counting/capacity evidence | Not an automatic global gate or an extra feature |
170: 
171: Production metered resume remains disabled until counter restoration is implemented and verified.
172: 
173: ## Change control
174: 
175: Internal class and function organization may vary while preserving shared record names, types, authority and failure semantics. Changes to public fields, source-validity rules, thresholds or shared dispatch/publication paths require a versioned contract/test revision and affected-owner review. Each feature requires its own approved plan, exact file scope and independent test design before implementation.

1: # ADR-001 — Deterministic extensions at existing application boundaries
2: 
3: Status: Proposed. Interface version: 1.0.
4: 
5: ## Context and drivers
6: 
7: The extension preserves the existing single-stock graph, model clients, data providers and publication paths. Architectural drivers are verifiable outputs, explicit degraded behavior, bounded dispatch, limited baseline changes and independent offline acceptance tests.
8: 
9: ## Decision process and alternatives
10: 
11: Trace the existing dispatch and publication paths, compare the candidates in the [evaluation table](../evaluation-table.md), define shared contracts and review adverse cases before implementation.
12: 
13: | Option | Assessment |
14: |---|---|
15: | Prompt and configuration changes only | Insufficient enforcement of publication, arithmetic, missing-data state and total request limits |
16: | Deterministic components at existing boundaries | Selected; supports the five acceptance contracts with localized integration |
17: | Replacement orchestration | Deferred; increases migration and regression scope without an identified requirement |

19: ## Component decisions
20: 
21: | Requirement | Decision |
22: |---|---|
23: | FR-01 | Resolve current-run evidence and apply one publication result at every official sink |
24: | FR-02 | Compute from validated operands; resolve immutable verified records by ID |
25: | FR-03 | Separate source coverage, assessment and execution state; 0/3 yields UNKNOWN/null without a sentiment-model call |
26: | NFR-01 | Atomically reserve capacity at a common outbound boundary |
27: | NFR-02 | Reduce optional history at the two scoped sites; reject irreducible messages before budget reservation |

29: Use [C0–C5](../interface-contracts.md) JSON-compatible shared records. Internal types may use adapters. Add separate owner keys to AgentState and retain legacy report strings as views of authoritative records.

31: ## Layered model context
32: 
33: Context layers are role/task identity, standing constraints, typed evidence and run state, active tool exchanges, optional discussion history and the current request. Mark required blocks explicitly.
34: 
35: Assembly order: prioritize and deduplicate optional history; measure the final representation; remove optional groups oldest first; reassemble; re-inject critical constraints; verify required blocks and tool pairs; recount before dispatch. Preserve authoritative stored evidence when reducing a request. Refuse a scoped request when mandatory content cannot fit.
36: 
37: NFR-02 uses a configurable 65536-byte message cap at analyst closure and the neutral risk role. It excludes separately bound tool schemas and is independent of token measurement.
38: 
39: ## Token-budget design
40: 
41: The input-token design uses a proposed cap of 16384 tokens and a compaction trigger above 13107 tokens (floor of 80% of the cap). Configure output allowance and provider-envelope reserve independently. Validate the selected model capacity, counting method, schema overhead and provider conversion before enabling this policy. Until then, token enforcement remains unverified. Byte counts are not a substitute for token counts.
42: 
43: ## Run profile
44: 
45: The initial product profile uses a configurable request limit of 40, both tiers on the school model alias, explicit thinking-disabled requests and an output allowance of 4096 tokens. NFR-01 boundary fixtures use limit 3. Configuration evidence accompanies baseline comparisons; changes to public semantics require a contract revision.
46: 
47: ## Consequences and review triggers
48: 
49: Benefits are localized changes and explicit failure states. Costs are shared dispatch/publication integration and nullable-state compatibility across existing consumers. Review this decision when provider retries become opaque, a sink bypasses publication checks, required context routinely cannot fit, or requirements need different orchestration.
50: 
51: Changes to shared fields, date semantics, thresholds, safety behavior or dependencies require affected-owner review and synchronized requirements, interfaces and tests. Record the human decision and supporting evidence.

1: """Deterministic publication gate for FR-01 / INV-01.
2: 
3: Owner module for the release decision described in
4: ``architecture-blueprint.md`` (FR-01 row) and ``docs/architecture/invariants.md``
5: (INV-01). The gate is the single authority for whether a candidate recommendation
6: becomes an official decision. Model text is advisory: only evidence links the
7: program itself verified in *this run* can back a release, and no free-text rating
8: fallback is honoured around the gate.
9: 
10: Design (plan revision 1):
11: - Evidence is indexed from the run's own non-empty analyst reports *before* the
12:   first debate turn, so every accepted argument cites material that exists in
13:   this run. The index is carried on the graph state as **plain, msgpack-safe
14:   data** (``evidence_index`` = a dict of primitive values), never as an object,
15:   so checkpointed runs can be saved and resumed.
16: - Bull/Bear submit structured ``evidence_ids``; the program validates each against
17:   the run index and only then mints a run-bound ``argument_id``.
18: - The Portfolio Manager selects from those accepted ``argument_ids``.
19: - ``evaluate`` checks the whole chain (recommendation -> accepted argument ->
20:   this run's material) and returns one ``GateOutcome``. ``apply`` projects that
21:   outcome onto the run state used by the sinks (CLI, API, reports, memory).
22: 
23: Only two outward rejection reasons exist: ``INVALID_RATING`` and
24: ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``. Missing, unparseable, unknown and cross-run references
25: all map to ``INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE``; when both the rating and the evidence fail,
26: ``INVALID_RATING`` takes precedence.

118: class EvidenceIndex:
119:     """Run-scoped evidence and accepted arguments (in-memory helper).
120: 
121:     Built at run start from its own reports; ``accept`` validates submissions.
122:     The graph state holds ``index_to_state(...)`` rather than this object, and
123:     ``evaluate`` reads either shape via :func:`as_index`.
124:     """
125: 
126:     def __init__(self, run_id: str, evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord]):
127:         self.run_id = run_id
128:         self._evidence = dict(evidence)
129:         self._arguments: dict[str, ArgumentRecord] = {}
130: 
131:     # --- evidence ---
132: 
133:     def has_evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> bool:
134:         return evidence_id in self._evidence
135: 
136:     def evidence(self, evidence_id: str) -> EvidenceRecord:
137:         return self._evidence[evidence_id]
138: 
139:     @property
140:     def evidence_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
141:         return tuple(self._evidence)
142: 
143:     @property
144:     def evidence_records(self) -> tuple[EvidenceRecord, ...]:
145:         return tuple(self._evidence.values())
146: 
147:     # --- accepted arguments ---
148: 
149:     def accept(self, argument: ArgumentRecord) -> bool:
150:         """Accept an argument iff every cited evidence id resolves in this run.
151: 
152:         Returns whether it was accepted. Rejection leaves the index unchanged;
153:         the caller must not mint an argument id for a rejected submission.
154:         """
155:         if not argument.evidence_ids:
156:             return False
157:         if any(eid not in self._evidence for eid in argument.evidence_ids):
158:             return False
159:         self._arguments[argument.argument_id] = argument
160:         return True
161: 
162:     def argument(self, argument_id: str) -> ArgumentRecord:
163:         return self._arguments[argument_id]
164: 
165:     def has_argument(self, argument_id: str) -> bool:
166:         return argument_id in self._arguments
167: 
168:     @property
169:     def argument_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
170:         return tuple(self._arguments)
171: 
172:     @property
173:     def argument_records(self) -> tuple[ArgumentRecord, ...]:
174:         return tuple(self._arguments.values())

177: def as_index(value) -> EvidenceIndex:
178:     """A read-only EvidenceIndex view of either an object or the state dict.
179: 
180:     ``evaluate`` accepts the graph state's serializable dict or an in-memory
181:     index, so the same logic serves tests and resumed checkpoints.
182:     """
183:     if isinstance(value, EvidenceIndex):
184:         return value
185:     if value is None:
186:         return EvidenceIndex(run_id="", evidence={})
187:     run_id = value.get("run_id", "")
188:     evidence = {
189:         item["id"]: EvidenceRecord(
190:             evidence_id=item["id"], source=item["source"],
191:             excerpt=item.get("excerpt", ""), run_id=run_id,
192:         )
193:         for item in value.get("evidence", [])
194:     }
195:     index = EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)
196:     for arg in value.get("arguments", []):
197:         index._arguments[arg["id"]] = ArgumentRecord(
198:             argument_id=arg["id"], speaker=arg.get("speaker", ""),
199:             text=arg.get("text", ""), evidence_ids=tuple(arg.get("evidence_ids", [])),
200:         )
201:     return index

204: def build_evidence_index(run_id: str, state) -> EvidenceIndex:
205:     """Index this run's non-empty analyst reports, one ``evidence_id`` per report.
206: 
207:     Only material actually present in the run is indexed. Deterministic: ids and
208:     iteration order follow the fixed analyst key order, never model text.
209:     """
210:     evidence: dict[str, EvidenceRecord] = {}
211:     for key in _ANALYST_REPORT_KEYS:
212:         text = state.get(key)
213:         if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
214:             continue
215:         evidence_id = f"ev:{run_id}:{key}"
216:         evidence[evidence_id] = EvidenceRecord(
217:             evidence_id=evidence_id, source=key, excerpt=_excerpt(text), run_id=run_id,
218:         )
219:     return EvidenceIndex(run_id=run_id, evidence=evidence)

223:     """The evidence IDs and their material, for the researcher prompt.

225:     The model may cite only these IDs; they are the program-built index for this
226:     run, so a cited ID resolves to actual run material.
227:     """

243: def _normalize_rating(value) -> str | None:
244:     """The canonical 5-tier rating for ``value``, or ``None`` if not allowed.
245: 
246:     Accepts a bare tier string (from structured output) or a rating value enum.
247:     ``REVIEW`` and any out-of-scale string are not allowed ratings.
248:     """
249:     if value is None:
250:         return None
251:     rating = getattr(value, "value", value)
252:     if not isinstance(rating, str):

257: def evaluate(index, candidate_rating, candidate_argument_ids) -> GateOutcome:
258:     """Check the full chain and return the one release decision for this run.
259: 
260:     ``index`` may be the state dict or an EvidenceIndex. Order matters: an invalid
261:     rating is reported before a missing chain, so a candidate that fails both
262:     returns ``INVALID_RATING``. No free-text fallback is consulted here.
263:     """
264:     idx = as_index(index)
265:     rating = _normalize_rating(candidate_rating)
266:     if rating is None:
267:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INVALID_RATING, rating=None)
268: 
269:     cited = tuple(a for a in (candidate_argument_ids or ()) if a)
270:     resolved: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
271:     for argument_id in cited:
272:         if not idx.has_argument(argument_id):
273:             continue
274:         argument = idx.argument(argument_id)
275:         for evidence_id in argument.evidence_ids:
276:             if idx.has_evidence(evidence_id):
277:                 resolved.append((argument_id, evidence_id, idx.evidence(evidence_id).source))
278:     if not resolved:
279:         return GateOutcome(status=BLOCKED, reason=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, rating=None)
280: 
281:     return GateOutcome(
282:         status=APPROVED, reason=None, rating=rating, resolved_chain=tuple(resolved),
283:     )

286: def apply(outcome: GateOutcome, final_state: dict) -> dict:
287:     """Project the gate outcome onto the run state consumed by every sink.
288: 
289:     On APPROVED the official rating and resolved chain are published and the
290:     candidate body becomes the official ``final_trade_decision``. On BLOCKED the
291:     returned state carries no candidate material at all — the candidate body,
292:     candidate rating and candidate argument ids are removed from the mapping, so
293:     the Python API's returned state cannot expose or re-derive the candidate. The
294:     only place ``REVIEW`` appears is the API's second tuple member (computed by the
295:     caller via ``run_rating``); ``final_rating`` is emptied here, not set to REVIEW.
296:     """
297:     status = outcome.status
298:     final_state["publication_status"] = status
299:     final_state["publication_reason"] = outcome.reason
300:     final_state["publication_chain"] = list(outcome.resolved_chain)
301: 
302:     if outcome.approved:
303:         body = final_state.get("candidate_decision") or final_state.get("final_trade_decision") or ""
304:         final_state["final_rating"] = outcome.rating
305:         final_state["final_trade_decision"] = body
306:         final_state.pop("candidate_decision", None)
307:         final_state.pop("candidate_rating", None)
308:         final_state.pop("candidate_argument_ids", None)
309:     else:
310:         # No candidate material leaks into the returned state: the body, its rating
311:         # and the ids it cited are all removed. ``final_rating`` is emptied rather
312:         # than set to REVIEW; REVIEW is the API's second tuple member only.
313:         final_state["final_rating"] = ""
314:         final_state["final_trade_decision"] = ""
315:         final_state.pop("candidate_decision", None)
316:         final_state.pop("candidate_rating", None)
317:         final_state.pop("candidate_argument_ids", None)
318:     return final_state

309:     def _memory_step(self, state):
310:         """The graph's Memory Log step, alongside the analysts (#1428): settle every

312:         trade date for the Portfolio Manager (#1251).

315:         so it runs beside the analysts instead of before them. A failure here
316:         does not end the run: the analysts' work is kept, the lessons already in
317:         the log are used, and the report says what could not be settled.

320:         try:

322:             done = self.settle_all_pending(wait=False)

324:                 note = (f"{len(done.failed)} past decision(s) could not be settled this run "
325:                         "and stay pending.")

420:     def publish(self, final_state: dict) -> str:

422:

424:         (CLI display, API return, report save, memory write). Verifies the chain
425:         recommendation -> accepted argument -> this run's material using the
426:         evidence index the graph already built; it never re-builds the index or
427:         accepts new arguments. Writes the outcome onto ``final_state`` and returns
428:         the publication status.

430:         The Portfolio Manager writes only internal candidate fields; on refusal
431:         ``apply`` removes the candidate body and sets no official rating, so no
432:         official field carries it.
433:         """
434:         # FR-01 / INV-01: read the Portfolio Manager's *candidate* (internal
435:         # fields only), not any official field. The gate's apply() is the sole
436:         # writer of the official rating/body.
437:         from tradingagents.graph.publication_gate import (
438:             apply,
439:             build_evidence_index,
440:             evaluate,

444:         if index is None:
445:             # No index means nothing can be verified; fall back to an empty one.
446:             index = build_evidence_index("no-index", final_state)

448:             index,

450:             final_state.get("candidate_argument_ids") or (),

455:     def stream_run(self, graph_input, **args):
456:         """Stream a run as ``(messages, state)`` pairs.
457: 
458:         ``messages`` are the agents' messages, the analysts' included. ``state``
459:         is the run's state after a top-level step; for a step inside an analyst's
460:         graph it is that analyst's report once filed, else None.
461: 
462:         Each analyst works in a graph of its own, and the run's state takes the
463:         analysts' reports only when the slowest has finished, so their messages
464:         and reports come from their own finished steps ("tasks") as they happen.
465:         """
466:         args = {**args, "stream_mode": ["values", "tasks"]}
467:         # The graph's own config serves every tool call, as in propagate(), even
468:         # when the process-wide config has changed since. Each step runs in the
469:         # run's context, so the caller keeps its own between steps.
470:         context = run_config_context(self.config)
471:         stream = context.run(self.graph.stream, graph_input, subgraphs=True, **args)
472:         try:
473:             while (step := context.run(next, stream, None)) is not None:
474:                 namespace, mode, chunk = step
475:                 if namespace:
476:                     result = chunk.get("result") if mode == "tasks" else None
477:                     if isinstance(result, dict):
478:                         report = {k: v for k, v in result.items() if k != "messages" and v}
479:                         if result.get("messages") or report:
480:                             yield result.get("messages", []), report or None
481:                 elif mode == "values":
482:                     yield chunk.get("messages", []), chunk
483:         finally:
484:             context.run(stream.close)

512: def extract_content_string(content):
513:     """Extract string content from various message formats.
514:     Returns None if no meaningful text content is found.
515:     """
516:     def is_empty(val):
517:         """Whether a value carries nothing to show.
518: 
519:         Text is judged by whether anything was written, not by what it would
520:         mean as Python: a report saying "0" or "None" is a message the run
521:         produced, and reading it as a falsy literal dropped it from the display.
522:         """
523:         if isinstance(val, str):
524:             return not val.strip()
525:         return val is None or not bool(val)
526: 
527:     if is_empty(content):
528:         return None
529: 
530:     if isinstance(content, str):
531:         return content.strip()
532: 
533:     if isinstance(content, dict):
534:         text = content.get('text', '')
535:         return text.strip() if not is_empty(text) else None
536: 
537:     if isinstance(content, list):
538:         text_parts = [
539:             item.get('text', '').strip() if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') == 'text'
540:             else (item.strip() if isinstance(item, str) else '')
541:             for item in content
542:         ]
543:         result = ' '.join(t for t in text_parts if t and not is_empty(t))
544:         return result if result else None
545: 
546:     return str(content).strip() if not is_empty(content) else None
547:

549: def classify_message_type(message) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
550:     """Classify LangChain message into display type and extract content.
551: 
552:     Returns:
553:         (type, content) - type is one of: User, Agent, Data, Control
554:                         - content is extracted string or None
555:     """
556:     from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage, ToolMessage
557: 
558:     content = extract_content_string(getattr(message, 'content', None))
559: 
560:     if isinstance(message, HumanMessage):
561:         if content and content.strip() == "Continue":
562:             return ("Control", content)
563:         return ("User", content)
564: 
565:     if isinstance(message, ToolMessage):
566:         return ("Data", content)
567: 
568:     if isinstance(message, AIMessage):
569:         return ("Agent", content)
570: 
571:     # Fallback for unknown types
572:     return ("System", content)

583: class AnalystWallTimeTracker:
584:     def __init__(self, plan: AnalystExecutionPlan):
585:         self.plan = plan
586:         self._started_at: dict[str, float] = {}
587:         self._wall_times: dict[str, float] = {}
588: 
589:     def mark_started(self, analyst_key: str, started_at: float | None = None) -> None:
590:         if analyst_key not in ANALYST_NODE_SPECS:
591:             raise ValueError(f"unknown analyst key: {analyst_key}")
592:         self._started_at.setdefault(analyst_key, monotonic() if started_at is None else started_at)
593: 
594:     def mark_completed(
595:         self,
596:         analyst_key: str,
597:         completed_at: float | None = None,
598:     ) -> None:
599:         if analyst_key not in ANALYST_NODE_SPECS:
600:             raise ValueError(f"unknown analyst key: {analyst_key}")
601:         if analyst_key in self._wall_times:
602:             return
603:         started_at = self._started_at.get(analyst_key)
604:         if started_at is None:
605:             return
606:         finished_at = monotonic() if completed_at is None else completed_at
607:         self._wall_times[analyst_key] = max(0.0, finished_at - started_at)
608: 
609:     def format_summary(self) -> str:
610:         parts = []
611:         for spec in self.plan.specs:
612:             duration = self._wall_times.get(spec.key)
613:             if duration is not None:
614:                 label = spec.agent_node.removesuffix(" Analyst")
615:                 parts.append(f"{label} {duration:.2f}s")
616:         if not parts:
617:             return "Analyst wall time: pending"
618:         return "Analyst wall time: " + " | ".join(parts)

621: def sync_analyst_tracker_from_chunk(
622:     tracker: AnalystWallTimeTracker,
623:     chunk: dict[str, str],
624:     now: float | None = None,
625: ) -> None:
626:     """The analysts start together; each stops its clock when its report lands."""
627:     current_time = monotonic() if now is None else now
628:     for spec in tracker.plan.specs:
629:         tracker.mark_started(spec.key, started_at=current_time)
630:         if chunk.get(spec.report_key):
631:             tracker.mark_completed(spec.key, completed_at=current_time)

97: def write_report_tree(final_state: dict, ticker: str, save_path, settings: dict | None = None,
98:                       html: bool = True) -> Path:
99:     """Save a completed run's reports to ``save_path``; return the complete-report path.
100: 
101:     ``settings`` (``TradingAgentsGraph.run_settings()``) adds what produced the run
102:     to the report's header. ``html`` also writes ``complete_report.html``, one
103:     self-contained page of the same report (#1419).
104:     Reusing a directory replaces the generated report files, removing sections
105:     absent from this run and disabled HTML. Other files and directories are kept.
106:     """
107:     save_path = Path(save_path)
108:     save_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
109:     parts = _report_parts(final_state)
110:     sections = []
111:     for heading, folder, written in parts:
112:         (save_path / folder).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
113:         for _agent, filename, text in written:
114:             (save_path / folder / filename).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
115:         content = "\n\n".join(f"### {agent}\n{text}" for agent, _filename, text in written)
116:         sections.append(f"## {heading}\n\n{content}")
117: 
118:     (save_path / "complete_report.md").write_text(
119:         _header(ticker, final_state, settings) + "\n\n".join(sections), encoding="utf-8"
120:     )
121:     if html:
122:         from tradingagents.report_html import render_report
123: 
124:         (save_path / "complete_report.html").write_text(
125:             render_report(ticker, final_state, settings, parts), encoding="utf-8"
126:         )
127:     else:
128:         (save_path / "complete_report.html").unlink(missing_ok=True)
129: 
130:     # Reconcile only the filenames owned by this writer; never clear the tree,
131:     # since callers may keep notes or other artifacts alongside the reports.
132:     current_files = {
133:         (folder, filename)
134:         for _heading, folder, written in parts
135:         for _agent, filename, _text in written
136:     }
137:     for _heading, folder, agents in _SECTIONS:
138:         for _agent, filename, _path in agents:
139:             if (folder, filename) not in current_files:
140:                 (save_path / folder / filename).unlink(missing_ok=True)
141:     return save_path / "complete_report.md"

32:     def store_decision(
33:         self,
34:         ticker: str,
35:         trade_date: str,
36:         final_trade_decision: str,
37:         rating: str | None = None,
38:     ) -> None:

40:

42:         one it is read from the decision text.

45:             return
46:         with locked(self._log_path):
47:             # Idempotency guard: fast raw-text scan instead of full parse. Any entry
48:             # for this ticker and date blocks another, pending or settled: a re-run
49:             # after the outcome landed would otherwise count the same decision twice
50:             # in past context and in every aggregate over the log.
51:             if self._log_path.exists():
52:                 raw = self._log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

58:             entry = f"{tag}\n\nDECISION:\n{final_trade_decision}{self._SEPARATOR}"

62:     def settling(self, wait: bool = True):

64:

66:         each and writes it; two passes at once would pay for the same
67:         reflections. A separate lock from the one each write takes. Yields
68:         whether it is held; with ``wait=False`` another pass is not waited for.

130:         if cross:

132:             parts.extend(self._format_reflection_only(e) for e in cross)

137:     def update_with_outcome(
138:         self,
139:         ticker: str,

153:         its tag with return figures (and the ``resolution_date`` the outcome

189:                     new_blocks.append(
190:                         f"{new_tag}\n\n{rest.lstrip()}\n\nREFLECTION:\n{reflection}"
191:                     )
192:                     updated = True
193:                 else:
194:                     new_blocks.append(block)

196:             if not updated:
197:                 return False
198: 
199:             new_blocks = self._apply_rotation(new_blocks)
200:             new_text = self._SEPARATOR.join(new_blocks)
201:             tmp_path = self._log_path.with_suffix(".tmp")
202:             tmp_path.write_text(new_text, encoding="utf-8")

206:     def batch_update_with_outcomes(self, updates: list[dict]) -> None:

211:         """
212:         if not self._log_path or not self._log_path.exists() or not updates:
213:             return
214:         with locked(self._log_path):
215:             text = self._log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
216:             blocks = text.split(self._SEPARATOR)

218:             update_map = {(u["trade_date"], u["ticker"]): u for u in updates}

220:             new_blocks = []
221:             for block in blocks:
222:                 stripped = block.strip()
223:                 if not stripped:
224:                     new_blocks.append(block)
225:                     continue
226: 
227:                 lines = stripped.splitlines()

230:                 matched = False

233:                     if tag_line.startswith(pending_prefix) and tag_line.endswith("| pending]"):
234:                         fields = [f.strip() for f in tag_line[1:-1].split("|")]
235:                         rating = fields[2]
236:                         raw_pct = f"{upd['raw_return']:+.1%}"

238:                         new_tag = self._resolved_tag(
239:                             trade_date, ticker, rating, raw_pct, alpha_pct,
240:                             upd["holding_days"], upd.get("resolution_date"),
241:                         )
242:                         rest = "\n".join(lines[1:])
243:                         new_blocks.append(
244:                             f"{new_tag}\n\n{rest.lstrip()}\n\nREFLECTION:\n{upd['reflection']}"
245:                         )
246:                         del update_map[(trade_date, ticker)]
247:                         matched = True
248:                         break
249: 
250:                 if not matched:
251:                     new_blocks.append(block)

253:             new_blocks = self._apply_rotation(new_blocks)
254:             new_text = self._SEPARATOR.join(new_blocks)
255:             tmp_path = self._log_path.with_suffix(".tmp")
256:             tmp_path.write_text(new_text, encoding="utf-8")
257:             tmp_path.replace(self._log_path)

259:     # --- Helpers ---
260: 
261:     @staticmethod
262:     def _resolved_tag(
263:         trade_date, ticker, rating, raw_pct, alpha_pct, holding_days, resolution_date
264:     ) -> str:
265:         """Build a resolved entry tag, recording the outcome's known-by date.
266: 
267:         ``resolution_date`` (the date of the last price bar used for the return)
268:         is the point-in-time cutoff a later run filters on (#1251). Omitted when
269:         unavailable, keeping the legacy 6-field tag.
270:         """
271:         tag = f"[{trade_date} | {ticker} | {rating} | {raw_pct} | {alpha_pct} | {holding_days}d"
272:         if resolution_date:
273:             tag += f" | resolved:{resolution_date}"
274:         return tag + "]"
275: 
276:     def _apply_rotation(self, blocks: list[str]) -> list[str]:
277:         """Drop the oldest-dated resolved blocks when their count exceeds max_entries.
278: 
279:         Pending blocks are always kept (they represent unprocessed work).
280:         Returns ``blocks`` unchanged when rotation is disabled or under cap.
281:         """
282:         if not self._max_entries or self._max_entries <= 0:
283:             return blocks
284: 
285:         # Tag each block with (block, is_resolved, decision date) from its tag line.
286:         decisions = []
287:         for block in blocks:
288:             stripped = block.strip()
289:             if not stripped:
290:                 decisions.append((block, False, ""))
291:                 continue
292:             tag_line = stripped.splitlines()[0].strip()
293:             is_resolved = (
294:                 tag_line.startswith("[")
295:                 and tag_line.endswith("]")
296:                 and not tag_line.endswith("| pending]")
297:             )
298:             decisions.append((block, is_resolved, tag_line[1:].split("|")[0].strip()))
299: 
300:         resolved_count = sum(1 for _, r, _ in decisions if r)
301:         if resolved_count <= self._max_entries:
302:             return blocks
303: 
304:         # The oldest by decision date, then by position: a backfill writes older
305:         # decisions last.
306:         resolved = [i for i, (_, is_resolved, _) in enumerate(decisions) if is_resolved]
307:         dated = sorted(resolved, key=lambda i: (decisions[i][2], i))
308:         dropped = set(dated[:resolved_count - self._max_entries])
309:         return [block for i, (block, _, _) in enumerate(decisions) if i not in dropped]
310: 
311:     def _parse_entry(self, raw: str) -> dict | None:
312:         lines = raw.strip().splitlines()
313:         if not lines:
314:             return None
315:         tag_line = lines[0].strip()
316:         if not (tag_line.startswith("[") and tag_line.endswith("]")):
317:             return None
318:         fields = [f.strip() for f in tag_line[1:-1].split("|")]
319:         if len(fields) < 4:
320:             return None
321:         # Optional trailing "resolved:YYYY-MM-DD" field records when the outcome
322:         # became known, for point-in-time filtering (#1251).
323:         resolved = None
324:         for f in fields[6:]:
325:             if f.startswith("resolved:"):
326:                 resolved = f[len("resolved:"):].strip()
327:         entry = {
328:             "date": fields[0],
329:             "ticker": fields[1],
330:             "rating": fields[2],
331:             "pending": fields[3] == "pending",
332:             "raw": fields[3] if fields[3] != "pending" else None,
333:             "alpha": fields[4] if len(fields) > 4 else None,
334:             "holding": fields[5] if len(fields) > 5 else None,
335:             "resolved": resolved,
336:         }
337:         body = "\n".join(lines[1:]).strip()
338:         decision_match = self._DECISION_RE.search(body)
339:         reflection_match = self._REFLECTION_RE.search(body)
340:         entry["decision"] = decision_match.group(1).strip() if decision_match else ""
341:         entry["reflection"] = reflection_match.group(1).strip() if reflection_match else ""
342:         return entry
343: 
344:     def _format_full(self, e: dict) -> str:
345:         raw = e["raw"] or "n/a"
346:         alpha = e["alpha"] or "n/a"
347:         holding = e["holding"] or "n/a"
348:         tag = f"[{e['date']} | {e['ticker']} | {e['rating']} | {raw} | {alpha} | {holding}]"
349:         parts = [tag, f"DECISION:\n{e['decision']}"]
350:         if e["reflection"]:
351:             parts.append(f"REFLECTION:\n{e['reflection']}")
352:         return "\n\n".join(parts)
353: 
354:     def _format_reflection_only(self, e: dict) -> str:
355:         tag = f"[{e['date']} | {e['ticker']} | {e['rating']} | {e['raw'] or 'n/a'}]"
356:         if e["reflection"]:
357:             return f"{tag}\n{e['reflection']}"
358:         text = e["decision"][:300]
359:         suffix = "..." if len(e["decision"]) > 300 else ""
360:         return f"{tag}\n{text}{suffix}"

1: """Shared 5-tier rating vocabulary and a deterministic heuristic parser.
2: 
3: The same five-tier scale (Buy, Overweight, Hold, Underweight, Sell) is used by:
4: - The Research Manager (investment plan recommendation)
5: - The Portfolio Manager (final position decision; its free-text fallback is read here)
6: - The memory log (rating tag stored alongside each decision entry)
7: 
8: Centralising it here avoids drift between those call sites.
9: 
10: ``extract_rating`` returns ``None`` when no rating can be found, and every
11: caller turns that into ``REVIEW`` rather than a tradeable position: a decision
12: nobody can read is not a Hold, and a Hold recorded in its place is quoted back to
13: the next run as a call that was never made (#1170).
14: """
15: 
16: from __future__ import annotations
17: 
18: import re
19: import unicodedata
20: 
21: # Canonical, ordered 5-tier scale (most bullish to most bearish).
22: RATINGS_5_TIER: tuple[str, ...] = (
23:     "Buy", "Overweight", "Hold", "Underweight", "Sell",
24: )
25: 
26: # Signal emitted when the model's decision has no recognizable rating. It is not
27: # a tradeable position: it flags output that needs a human/re-run rather than
28: # silently degrading to Hold. Callers that map the signal onto the 5-tier enum
29: # (e.g. ``PortfolioRating(signal)``) should guard with ``is_review`` first.
30: RATING_REVIEW = "REVIEW"
31: 
32: _RATING_SET = {r.lower() for r in RATINGS_5_TIER}
33: 
34: # Matches "Rating: X" / "rating - X" / "Rating — **X**" — tolerates markdown
35: # bold wrappers and any dash or colon a model writes as the separator. "rating"
36: # must start a word, so "Operating margin: Sell-side" is not a label.
37: _RATING_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![a-z])rating\b[^:\-\u2010-\u2015]*[:\-\u2010-\u2015][\s*]*(\w+)",
38:                               re.IGNORECASE)
39: 
40: # The decision's own rating line, in the shape the Portfolio Manager is asked to
41: # open with ("- **Rating**: X", "**Final Rating**: X", "## Our rating - X"): an
42: # optional list marker, emphasis and heading marks, and only words naming the
43: # decision itself before "rating". "Consensus rating: Buy" or "Trader's rating:
44: # Buy" is someone else's rating.
45: _OWN_QUALIFIER = r"(?:(?:final|our|overall|my|recommended|updated|revised|new|current)\s+)*"
46: _RATING_LINE_RE = re.compile(
47:     r"\s*(?P<item>(?:[-+*\u2022]|\d+[.)])\s+)?[\s*_#]*" + _OWN_QUALIFIER
48:     + r"rating[^\w:\-\u2010-\u2015]*[:\-\u2010-\u2015][\s*]*(?P<value>\w+)",
49:     re.IGNORECASE,
50: )
51: 
52: # A line presenting the scale rather than a decision ("Rating Scale: Buy, ...").
53: _RATING_SCALE_RE = re.compile(r"rating\s*(scale|options|legend)", re.IGNORECASE)
54: 
55: def extract_rating(text: str) -> str | None:
56:     """Extract a 5-tier rating from its label, or ``None`` if there is none.
57: 
58:     Reads an explicit "Rating: X" label (tolerant of markdown bold) in the
59:     NFKC-normalized text, so fullwidth punctuation like ``Rating：Overweight``
60:     matches as ASCII does: the decision's opening rating line, else its own
61:     rating lines or, failing those, every label, when they agree.
62:     """
63:     if not text:
64:         return None
65:     norm = unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", text)
66: 
67:     # The decision is asked to open with its rating, so a first line (after any
68:     # headings) in that shape is the call. A list item there may also be a quote
69:     # heading a list of other parties' ratings, so it counts with the decision's
70:     # other rating lines, which leave out list items; failing those, every label
71:     # counts. Either way they must agree: ratings that differ, with nothing
72:     # marking which one is the call, are no call (#1170). Lines presenting the
73:     # scale itself are a legend the model echoed, not a call.
74:     lines = [line for line in norm.splitlines() if line.strip() and not _RATING_SCALE_RE.search(line)]
75:     first = next((line for line in lines if not line.lstrip().startswith("#")
76:                   or _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)), "")
77:     m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(first)
78:     opening = m if m and m.group("value").lower() in _RATING_SET else None
79:     if opening and not opening.group("item"):
80:         return opening.group("value").capitalize()
81: 
82:     own = [opening.group("value").capitalize()] if opening else []
83:     labels = []
84:     for line in lines:
85:         m = _RATING_LINE_RE.match(line)
86:         if m and not m.group("item") and m.group("value").lower() in _RATING_SET:
87:             own.append(m.group("value").capitalize())
88:         labels += [v.capitalize() for v in _RATING_LABEL_RE.findall(line) if v.lower() in _RATING_SET]
89:     # Without a label there is no call to read: a rating word in the prose may be
90:     # one the text argues against ("not a Sell"), and reading it reports a
91:     # direction nobody decided.
92:     found = own or labels
93:     return found[0] if found and len(set(found)) == 1 else None
94: 
95: 
96: def parse_rating(text: str, default: str = RATING_REVIEW) -> str:
97:     """Extract a 5-tier rating, or ``REVIEW`` when the decision has none.
98: 
99:     For callers that need a string for every decision, such as the memory log's
100:     entry tag. The default is the review sentinel, never a tradeable rating.
101:     """
102:     rating = extract_rating(text)
103:     return rating if rating is not None else default
104: 
105: 
106: def run_rating(final_state: dict) -> str:
107:     """A finished run's rating: the Portfolio Manager's own, else read from its decision.
108: 
109:     The fallback serves a state without ``final_rating``, such as a run an older
110:     version completed and a checkpoint hands back unchanged.
111:     """
112:     return final_state.get("final_rating") or parse_rating(final_state.get("final_trade_decision", ""))
113: 
114: 
115: def is_review(signal: str) -> bool:
116:     """Whether a signal is the non-tradeable REVIEW sentinel (#1170)."""
117:     return signal == RATING_REVIEW
